title: Etale scheme charts of a discrete finite-type DM stack over a field
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Stacks, Deligne--Mumford stacks, representability by algebraic spaces and 2-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, def-trf-algebraic-space]. An etale chart is a representable-by-algebraic-spaces etale map from a scheme, and an atlas is a surjective chart; etale and smooth are tested on scheme charts using [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] over $S$ and let $\mathcal Z$ be a Deligne--Mumford stack over $k$. Suppose that $\mathcal Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type, meaning locally of finite type on smooth scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and that $|\mathcal Z|$ is discrete. Here the point space consists of field-valued objects modulo isomorphism after common field extension, with topology detected by any smooth surjective scheme atlas. For every etale scheme chart $A\to\mathcal Z$, not necessarily surjective, the composite $A\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite].

source.place: Tag 06UC (lemma-locally-quasi-finite-over-field), etale-chart specialization; its proof uses only local finite type, discreteness of the stack point space, and local quasi-finiteness of the chart.

proof.text: Write $a:A\to\mathcal Z$. The chartwise calculus makes $a$ smooth and locally of finite type. The stack finite-type calculus then makes $A\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ locally of finite type. Set $R=A\times_{\mathcal Z}A$, with projections $s,t:R\to A$. This is an algebraic space by representability of $a$, and both projections are etale by base change. These assertions do not require $a$ to be surjective.

source.place: Tag 06UC (lemma-locally-quasi-finite-over-field), proof specialized to etale charts; only its stated local finite type, discrete point space, and chart quasi-finiteness inputs are used.

proof.text: Assume that $A\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is not locally quasi-finite. The specialization lemma gives distinct $v,v^{\prime}\in A$ with $v\leadsto v^{\prime}$, and the strict-drop lemma gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(v)>\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(v^{\prime})$. Continuity of $|a|$ sends this specialization to one in $|\mathcal Z|$. A discrete space has no specialization between distinct points, so $|a|(v)=|a|(v^{\prime})$.

source.place: Tag 06UC (lemma-locally-quasi-finite-over-field), proof specialized to etale charts; only its stated local finite type, discrete point space, and chart quasi-finiteness inputs are used.

proof.text: The equality of point classes means that their residue-field representatives become 2-isomorphic over a common field extension $L$. The two maps $\operatorname{Spec}L\to A$, with that isomorphism over $\mathcal Z$, are an object of the 2-fibre product $R$. Its point $r\in|R|$ satisfies $s(r)=v$ and $t(r)=v^{\prime}$. This is the direct construction in Tag 04XH (lemma-points-cartesian), using the stated definition of point classes and the defining triples of the 2-fibre product.

source.place: Tag 06UC (lemma-locally-quasi-finite-over-field), proof specialized to etale charts; only its stated local finite type, discrete point space, and chart quasi-finiteness inputs are used.

proof.text: Choose an etale scheme chart $W\to R$ and $w\in W$ above $r$, using the point-surjectivity of an etale scheme cover of an algebraic space. Since $s$ and $t$ are etale, the etale-space lemma makes both locally quasi-finite. Apply the chart transcendence-degree comparison to $R\xrightarrow{s}A\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $R\xrightarrow{t}A\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, with the same $W,w$. It gives $$\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(v)=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(w)=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(v^{\prime}).$$ The required local finite type of $A/k$ was established in step 1.

source.place: Tag 06UC (lemma-locally-quasi-finite-over-field), proof specialized to etale charts; only its stated local finite type, discrete point space, and chart quasi-finiteness inputs are used.

proof.text: The equality in step 4 contradicts the strict inequality in step 2. Thus $A\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally quasi-finite. Since the chart $a$ was arbitrary, this proves the assertion for every chart, including the empty chart.
